business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Headline self-description is a "One order a Day company", with the added claim that it "continued to securing one exports order every quarter".
- Order book as on 30.06.2026 is called the "Highest Ever Order book at Rs 9445 crore", with "Rs 670+ crore of new orders (Incl. extension)" added during the quarter.
- Order book is split "Nomination vs Competition" at Nomination 38% and Competition 62%, indicating a mix of government-nominated and competitively won work.
- Signed an MoU "with CRISIL for integrated, data-driven infrastructure solutions".
- Client roster in the quarter spans central/state and PSU bodies — Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, NALCO, Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power, Mormugao Port Authority, Steel Authority of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, Northern Railways — plus an overseas client, Medha Mobility Australia Pty. Limited.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Major contracts secured Q1FY27] Largest disclosed wins are Project Management Consultancy for Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Lucknow at Rs 169 Cr (completion 2028); NALCO PMC extension for the Sankerjang railway siding, Orissa at Rs 39 Cr (2026); Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power locomotive wet-lease and siding O&M at Rs 29 Cr (2030); Mormugao Port Authority locomotive hire at Rs 21 Cr (2031); SAIL WDS6 locomotive overhauling at Bokaro at Rs 20 Cr (2028); Ministry of Home Affairs third-party inspection of ICBR-II roads at Rs 16 Cr (2029); Medha Mobility Australia locomotive supply at Rs 9 Cr (2026); and a Northern Railways Delhi station decongestion study at Rs 8 Cr (2027).
- [Employee productivity] Revenue per employee is shown as 0.99, 1.06, 0.97, 0.87 and 0.90 (Rs Cr) for FY22-FY26 and 0.18 for both Q1FY26 and Q1FY27; PAT per employee is 0.19, 0.21, 0.18, 0.15, 0.15 for FY22-FY26 and 0.025 for both Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 — standalone, based on the average quarterly employee count.
- [Restatement] "Due to reclassification of reversal of provisions from other operating income to expenses, revenue have been restated in Q1FY26", applied to both total and segmental revenue, so year-on-year comparisons in the deck are against a restated base.
- [Unallocable expenses] Segmental profit table carries un-allocable expenses of Rs 36 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 32 crore in Q1FY26, i.e. segment profits shown do not net down to reported profit.
- [Internal contradiction] The round-up slide says the quarter added "Rs 670+ crore of new orders (Incl. extension)" while the order book slide states "Rs 674 Crore" and "including extensions of Rs 674 crore"; both readings are as printed.

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
